epics.title: AWS and required Cloudflare provisioning
epics.intent: Support two explicit installation profiles: managed ECS Fargate plus private managed PostgreSQL, and a small EC2 VM running the app plus owner-hosted PostgreSQL. Qualify the managed profile first in S2, then the small-VM profile in S3/S4. Cloudflare is required in both. Each profile has independent cost, availability, credentials, backup, deployment and live-evidence contracts; switching profiles is an explicit data migration.
exit_criteria: Both profiles have separate cost/resource inventories and passing qualification. Managed service costs, single-VM operational burden and all retained resources are visible without assuming free-tier credits.
Resources use owner-controlled encrypted Pulumi state; provider authentication is explicit and Cloudflare DNS-only and proxy modes remain separate contracts.
No direct host PostgreSQL exposure, embedded cloud keys or destructive default exists. E16 owns explicitly authorized live DNS, TLS, deployment and restore evidence.

findings: Both AWS profiles are confirmed scope: managed containers plus managed PostgreSQL, and a small VM with app plus PostgreSQL, selected per installation. Profile switching is an explicit migration, not a setting change.

AMSL public candidate components provide ECS Fargate immutable-digest deployment and private encrypted RDS, which fit the managed profile. They do not establish a ready-made small-VM Podman/PostgreSQL profile or executed AMOS adoption.
AMSL cloudflare/dnsalias is DNS-only and explicitly rejects proxied=true. Required Cloudflare participation can be satisfied by DNS-only; proxy/CDN/WAF capability needs a distinct qualified contract.

AMSL container-artifact uses Docker Buildx and infrastructure-preview requires a Pulumi access token. Podman plus owner-controlled state require explicit local composition or separately authorized upstream changes.
State, application database, backup data and recovery keys need distinct ownership and teardown protection. Pulumi state recovery does not recover application data.
Managed profile is sequenced for S2 qualification first; small-vm implementation follows in S3 with independent S4 qualification. This ordering does not remove either supported profile.
Cloud work depends on owner account/domain access, scoped credentials, budget/profile choices, DNS/TLS readiness and CI trust. Those are external gates, not coding throughput.
All listed checks are planned future checks. No implementation, build, deployment, release, provider mutation or live consumer test was performed by this planning work.
Root owns go.mod/go.sum, root .github workflow registration, CLI entrypoint and shared schema registries. These lanes produce bounded packages, templates and fragments for integration.

Exact scoped Go tests are implemented in the task-owned *_test.go paths. T1.5 supplies scripts/test-browser.sh; T1.6 supplies public artifact validation; T1.8 supplies the Go-check harness. Renderer should reconcile script flags with those frozen root contracts.
Future-stage tasks are fully inventoried by explicit request, but remain provisional and must be reconciled with frozen interfaces and prior-stage evidence before dispatch.

SES sender identity, region, DNS/DKIM, scoped runtime IAM, sandbox restrictions and real authorized receipt are separate E8.27-E8.28 qualification gates; T5.10 may consume them without depending on combined E16.
